children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--There were declines in Intercontinental Exchange canola futures late Friday morning, due to pressure from some comparable oils.
Soyoil down hard again

Along with another round losses in the Chicago soy complex, canola was getting pressured by declines crude oil. That was tempered somewhat by upticks in Malaysian palm oil, while European rapeseed was narrowly mixed.
Although crude oil was lower, an analyst said its futures were still above US$90 per barrel, which was supportive to canola.
Exports decline
Canola exports shrunk during the week ended Aug. 30, as the Canadian Grain Commission reported 58,300 tons left the country. That's down from 118,100 tons the previous week.
The analyst said that's normal for this time of year with elevators getting ready for the coming harvest. Once that does get underway, the analyst expects a change.
"We're going to be off to a strong start in terms of exports," he said.
Harvest
Saskatchewan reported its canola harvest was 4% complete with early yields at 38 bushels per acre.
Alberta is scheduled to release its latest crop report Friday afternoon.
India

There's to be slightly more rapeseed grown in India during 2026-27, the United States Department of Agriculture attache in New Delhi forecasted. That's to rise to 12.1 million tons from 11.9 million in 2025-26.
Loonie
The Canadian dollar was retreating late Friday morning, with the loonie falling to 72.27 U.S. cents, compared to Thursday's close of 72.52.
Closed Monday
The Canadian and U.S. markets will be closed on Monday for Labour Day.
